# Pandamonium v1.0.52

This release ships the full built-in tool catalog for the agent plus a small sidebar polish pass.

Agent turns now mount every enabled built-in tool, `manage_settings list_tools` reports the real catalog, and `load_tools` mounts any tool on demand for the remainder of a request. In the sidebar, bucket headers are flush left again at rest — the drag handle reveals itself only on hover and slides the label aside instead of permanently reserving a column — and the Projects section no longer prints instruction text under its header when it is empty.

## MAD-905 — Agent: uncap the built-in tool catalog (full native reach for API engines)

### Problem

The Built-in Tools panel catalogs 80 tools, but API turns mounted only the RAG-selected subset (a live session showed 23 of 80) and `manage_settings list_tools` returned a hardcoded summary instead of the real catalog. The agent could not invoke two-thirds of its own tools and often concluded a tool was missing.

### Implementation

API-host engines mount every enabled built-in schema each round; per-turn intent clamps stay authoritative and the measured tool-catalog budget (`cap_tool_schemas`) is the only trim. `manage_settings action=list_tools` returns the real catalog with id, category, description, and enabled state. `generate_image` and `manage_research` gained native schemas and `tail_serve_output` a toggle, closing the catalog/callable parity drift.

### Product value and UI visibility

No UI change. Every tool the Built-in Tools panel lists as enabled is now actually callable by the agent, and "how many tools do you have?" is answered from live state.

### Verification

`tests/test_agent_tool_catalog_uncap.py` covers full API mounting, disabled-tool respect, intent-clamp preservation, the real catalog listing, and parity; 212 focused tests passed on the feature branch alongside compile and diff hygiene checks, and the fix rode the v1.0.51/v1.0.52 head through the full CI suite.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No new dependency or configuration. The catalog is still bounded by the measured tool-schema budget, so a very large catalog can still be trimmed under pressure.

### References

- [Linear MAD-905](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-905/agent-uncap-the-built-in-tool-catalog-full-native-tool-reach-for-api)
- [Catalog PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/105)

## MAD-907 — Agent: on-demand tool catalog mount for local/text engines (MAD-905 Part 2/2)

### Problem

Local and text engines never received most of the built-in catalog. When such an engine needed a tool it could not see, the run dead-ended instead of letting the model discover and mount what it needed.

### Implementation

`manage_settings action=load_tools` mounts any enabled built-in tool for the remainder of the request and returns its exact fenced-block usage so text/local engines can format the call immediately. The agent loop unions a result's mounted tools into its selection and ranks mounted names ahead of the budget cap. The discovery gateway (`manage_settings`) stays available on every turn so a capped engine can always list and mount what it needs; network-inspection turns keep the gateway out via the existing allowlist clamp.

### Product value and UI visibility

No UI change. Text and local engines can now discover, mount, and call catalog tools mid-run instead of reporting a tool as unavailable.

### Verification

`tests/test_tool_catalog_mount.py` covers load/mount validation, budget-cap recovery, and selection unioning; 244 focused tests passed on the feature branch, and the change rode the v1.0.52 head through the full CI suite.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No new dependency or configuration. Mounts last for the current request only; the existing network-inspection allowlist behavior is preserved.

### References

- [Linear MAD-907](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-907/mad-905-agent-localtext-engine-on-demand-tool-catalog-mount-part-22)
- [Mount PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/119)

## MAD-908 — UI: keep bucket headers flush and drop the Projects empty-state copy

### Problem

The bucket drag handle introduced with section reordering occupied layout space even while invisible. Every sidebar section icon and label was pushed right by the reserved handle column, which read as a misalignment against the rest of the sidebar. Separately, an empty Projects section rendered an instruction sentence under the header that cluttered the list.

### Implementation

The handle is now absolutely positioned inside the section header, contributes no layout width, and is pointer-transparent at rest so it cannot intercept a click meant for the section title. Hovering or keyboard-focusing a header reveals the handle and transitions the label right by the handle width; leaving restores it. Rearrange mode keeps the shifted layout so the handle never overlaps the label. The Projects empty-state element and its render/error copy were removed; an empty section shows only its header and the add control.

### Product value and UI visibility

Sidebar icons and labels line up exactly as they did before reordering was added. The affordance is discoverable on hover without permanently costing alignment, and the Projects list is quiet when empty.

### Verification

`tests/test_bucket_header_flush.py` guards the overlay positioning, the hover slide, the pointer-events behavior, and the removed empty-state markup. The browser check in `tests/browser/mad-899-ui-batch.spec.js` measures the label position at rest versus on hover, asserts the handle opacity transition, and asserts no `#projects-empty` element exists.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Frontend-only CSS/markup/JS change with no data, schema, or API impact. Touch layouts already hid the handle and are unchanged. No new dependency.

### References

- [Linear MAD-908](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-908/ui-keep-bucket-headers-flush-and-drop-the-projects-empty-state-copy)
- [Fix PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/117)

## MAD-911 — Extensions: define the capability inventory, lazy-mount, and scan contracts

### Problem

Extensions had no shared contract for what an installed capability provides. There was no revision-bound inventory describing a capability's kind, permission mode, descriptor class, or schema; no defined rules for when inventory metadata must be treated as stale or tampered; no per-turn lazy-mount semantics for requesting schemas without flooding the first load; and no bounded static-scan artifact that a reviewer can trust before a package is enabled.

### Implementation

Contract checkpoint (M13 S0) defining three strict contracts: a revision-bound advisory capability inventory bound to `manifest_digest` + `inventory_digest` with fail-closed staleness/tamper rules, explicit separation from live `effective_capabilities`, and a schema-free advisory projection; per-turn lazy-mount schema resolution gated on the enabled registry record, engagement, and the executor allowlist; and a bounded static scan artifact with a stage enum and progress events, strict draft-manifest validation, file/byte/time bounds, mandatory evidence redaction, and a no-repository-execution boundary. Strict JSON schemas and pure validator/build helpers accompany the specs.

### Product value and UI visibility

No runtime or UI behavior change in this slice. It pins the contracts and schemas that the following M13 slices implement, so the inventory, lazy-mount, and scan surfaces cannot drift from the documented boundaries.

### Verification

Contract tests cover the strict validators, inventory/effective separation, digest binding, staleness and tamper fail-closed behavior, lazy-mount gating, and scan-artifact bounds and redaction. The change is contract-only with no runtime path modified and rode the v1.0.52 head through the full CI suite.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Contract-only: no registry, adapter, route, agent-tool, or UI behavior change. No new dependency. The static scan remains the only pre-enable artifact; MCP probing stays the single explicit runtime verification.

### References

- [Linear MAD-911](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-911/extensions-define-the-capability-inventory-lazy-mount-and-scan)
- [Contract PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/122)

## MAD-912 — Extensions: persist revision-bound capability inventory across disable and restart

### Problem

A disabled or restarted extension lost all visibility into what it could do: inventory lived only in live adapter state, so the operator could not inspect an installed capability while the extension was disabled, and a restart required re-running adapters to rebuild metadata that should be durable.

### Implementation

Registry records now carry the advisory capability inventory built by the MAD-911 contract. Preview/install extracts inventory per adapter — admitted skill metadata for skill bundles, resolved catalog names and schemas from the MCP probe, and declared capabilities/schemas for web inline/live catalogs. `disable()` clears live effective capabilities and admitted skills but keeps the inventory; restart rehydrates it from the lifecycle record without running adapters for disabled extensions. Inventory stays bound to source revision and manifest digest, and tampered or stale inventories are reported as absent while separately validated effective capabilities keep their existing authority. A bounded `capability_inventory()` read surface exposes names, kinds, permission modes, and counts only.

### Product value and UI visibility

No UI change. Installed extensions stay inspectable while disabled and after restart, and the operator-facing read payload contains no secrets, absolute paths, or private endpoints.

### Verification

`tests/test_extension_capability_inventory_persistence.py` covers installed-then-disabled inventory with empty effective capabilities, restart rehydration without adapter runs, tamper and staleness fail-closed behavior, and sanitized read payloads; existing suites stay green.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No new dependency; the registry-record shape is additive and a disabled inventory grants no execution path.

### References

- [Linear MAD-912](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-912/extensions-persist-revision-bound-capability-inventory-across-disable)
- [Persistence PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/129)
